speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; can you tell me how long you have had this symptom and if it is itchy?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Contact Dermatitis. The clinical presentation of a chronic, pruritic rash on the upper extremities that worsens with exposure, combined with the patient's history of no new medications or systemic illnesses, strongly suggests a localized allergic reaction to environmental contactants like soaps, detergents, or plants.
